blocks.title: 1. What is a Fraction?
blocks.content:
A fraction shows a **part of a whole**.

Imagine you have a whole pizza and you cut it into equal slices. If you take a slice, you have a fraction of the pizza!

We write fractions with a number on top and a number on the bottom.

blocks.title: 2. Numerator & Denominator
blocks.content:
Every fraction has two parts:

• **Numerator (Top Number):** How many parts we *have* or are talking about.
• **Denominator (Bottom Number):** How many *equal parts* make up the whole.

*(Tip to remember: **D**enominator is **D**own at the bottom!)*

blocks.title: 3. Types of Fractions
blocks.content:
Fractions come in different shapes and sizes:

• **Proper Fraction:** The top is smaller than the bottom (like 1/2 or 3/4). It's less than a whole.
• **Improper Fraction:** The top is bigger than or equal to the bottom (like 5/4). It's a whole or more!
• **Mixed Number:** A whole number plus a proper fraction (like 1 ½).
• **Equivalent Fractions:** Fractions that look different but show the exact same amount (like 1/2 and 2/4).

blocks.title: 4. Fraction Challenge
blocks.content:
You're getting good at this!

When comparing fractions with the **same bottom number** (denominator), just look at the top number. The bigger the top, the bigger the fraction.

If the top numbers are the same, the fraction with the **smaller bottom** is actually bigger, because the pieces are larger!

blocks.title: 5. Real-World Fractions
blocks.content:
Fractions are everywhere around us!

We use them when baking, telling time, sharing food, and measuring things.

Now that you've discovered fractions in the real world, you are ready for the test!
